subject: POC kickoff recap — scope, metrics, owners
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, John Patel <j.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff recap — scope, metrics, owners

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Recap below so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps for the POC kickoff. Please flag any corrections.

Goal of the POC
- Validate that Redwood's inference platform can reduce per-token cost by ~30% vs your current endpoint while maintaining output quality for customer support summarization flows.
- Demonstrate stable 100ms median latency for 512-token responses at 50 concurrent users.

Primary pain points you shared
- High variable cost during peak hours (support traffic spikes)
- Inconsistent latency causing timeouts in the UI
- Lack of reliable A/B evaluation tooling for prompt regressions

Scope and deliverables (4-week POC)
- Ingest sample support transcripts (up to 100k tokens/day) — Acme will provision staging S3 and a small anonymized dataset.
- Deploy Redwood hosted POC with model variants (open-llama-13B q4, redwood-rlhf-rl) and a fallback smaller model for cost/capacity tests.
- Provide prompt/eval suite for 10 representative prompts with pass/fail thresholds and qualitative examples.
- Run latency/load tests (50, 100, 200 concurrent simulated users) and provide performance report.

Success metrics
- >=30% reduction in per-token cost for production-grade throughput (measured over a 24h simulated peak)
- Median latency <=100ms at 50 concurrent users for 512-token responses
- No regressions on prompt eval set (precision threshold 0.85)

Owners and roles
- Acme: Samantha Lee (Product Owner), John Patel (Engineering lead), Alex Rivera (Data/ETL)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program owner), Aditya Rao (SE – infra/setup), Neha Kapoor (CS – onboarding & evals)

Initial timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Access & staging credentials, sign SOW draft, kickoff call (we can do a 30-min tech setup with Aditya)
- Week 1: Ingest sample data, configure prompt set, baseline run on your current endpoint
- Week 2: Redwood hosted tests (latency + cost runs), iterate prompts/quantization settings
- Week 3: Final report + extended run for 24h peak simulation, review next steps (Dedicated/Private options)

Access/setup items we need from Acme
- Staging S3 credentials (read-only for sample data) or a one-off transfer link for anonymized transcripts
- List of 10 representative prompts + expected outputs (example pairs)
- Allowlist IP ranges or a short-lived SSH key if we need to pull data into our test runners

Attachments: Redwood-ACME-POC-SOW-v1.pdf (SOW draft), redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (technical checklist) — both attached and uploaded to the Drive link below.

Next steps
- Samantha: share staging S3 creds and prompt examples by EOD Friday
- John/ Alex: confirm a 30-min tech setup window next Tue/Wed for Aditya
- Marissa/Neha: we’ll send calendar invites for kickoff and the tech setup

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: POC kickoff recap — scope, metrics, owners

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications: 

- On the success metrics: the 30% cost reduction target is relative to our current managed endpoint spend. We'll run a baseline this week and share the numbers.
- Data retention & privacy: legal asked whether Redwood can guarantee logs retention only for the duration of the POC and that transcripts will not be used to train models. Can you confirm?
- Access: we'll share a temporary staging S3 bucket and a service account key. Alex will send details.

We can do the tech setup on Tue 11/10 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for Aditya?

Thanks — Sam

Thanks Sam — Tue 11/10 10:00 AM PT works for me. Quick technical notes ahead of the setup so the call can be focused: 

Access & onboarding checklist (high level)
- Staging S3: read-only access preferred. If you provide a short-lived presigned link for the initial transfer that also works. Please include a small sample manifest.csv with file-level metadata so our ingest job can map fields.
- API keys: we’ll create a scoped API key for the POC with no retention beyond the contract period; confirm that you want logs deleted after the POC. Our default for POC is 90-day retention unless otherwise requested — we can set to "P0-delete" on contract execute.
- Network: if you prefer IP allowlisting, we can provide a set of IPs and a short-lived SSH key for initial pull.
- Model variants: we’ll initially spin up the two variants Marissa mentioned. For quantization testing we’ll need to push sample binaries; should be fine during Week 2.

Tech setup call agenda (30 mins)
1) Intros + roles (5m)
2) Walk through sample dataset and manifest (5m)
3) Show Redwood test runner and baseline capture (10m)
4) Confirm S3, keys, and timeline (5m)
5) Q&A / next steps (5m)

Links & attachments
- POC Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodAcmePOC
- Baseline script & runner (attached in Drive)

Privacy/legal note
- Neha (cc) is handling the privacy & retention addendum. Short answer: Redwood does not use POC data to train models without explicit opt-in and we can configure ephemeral retention for the POC. We’ll confirm exact language in the SOW.

Looking forward to the call.

—Aditya

- Legal/Privacy: I will update the SOW language to include a POC-only data retention clause (delete logs at POC end) and a clause that POC data is not used for training unless Acme provides explicit written opt-in. I aim to send the redline by EOD Mon 11/09.
- Onboarding & evals: I’ll own the prompt/eval suite — please send the 10 representative prompts + expected outputs to me (neha.kapoor@redwood.ai).
- Tech setup: Aditya will run the Tue 11/10 10:00 AM PT call (calendar invite sent).

Acme action items

We’ll use the Drive folder above for artifacts and I’ll update the checklist as items complete. Looking forward to getting started.
